✈️ LOOKING FOR YOUR NEXT ADVENTURE? 🚀
Ever wondered what it’s like to fly, glide, shoot, camp, take part in adventure training, learn first aid, compete in sports and challenge yourself in new ways?

Then come and see what the Royal Air Force Air Cadets are all about! 🇬🇧
🎯 OPEN DAY – WEDNESDAY 14TH OCTOBER
📍 40F (Maidstone) Squadron
📌 Boxley Road, Maidstone, ME14 2AR

If you're aged 12–17, this could be your chance to join an organisation where you can:
✈️ Experience aviation and potentially take to the skies
🪂 Get involved in gliding
🏕️ Take part in camps, expeditions and adventure activities
🏆 Develop skills through sports and challenges
🎖️ Learn leadership, teamwork and discipline
🏅 Work towards your Duke of Edinburgh’s Award
⛑️ Gain valuable first-aid and life skills
👥 Make new friends and become part of a team
You don't need to know anything about aviation or have any previous experience — just bring your enthusiasm and a willingness to give things a go!

Fill in the joining interest form (https://www.raf.mod.uk/aircadets/interested-in-joining-as-a-cadet/?squadronno=40F&id=7EB60CCD-B141-454B-9ED04F42DF0974CC) to express your interest and we'll invite you to come along on 14th October, meet the team, see what we're about and find out where being an Air Cadet could take you.

👉 Your next adventure could start here.

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc #RoyalAirForceAirCadets #RAFAC #40FMaidstone #Maidstone #YouthActivities #Adventure #Flying #openday  #Leadership #DofE #JoinUs #OpenDay

🏔️ SECTOR 3 CADETS TAKE ON INITIAL EXPEDITION TRAINING! 🏔️

What a weekend it has been! 🌄

This weekend, our Cadets  joined fellow Cadets from across Sector 3 for an action-packed Initial Expedition Training weekend — with almost 40 Cadets coming together from six fantastic Squadrons:

✈️ 40F (Maidstone)
✈️ 1039 (Gillingham)
✈️ 1404 (Chatham)
✈️ 25 (Parkwood)
✈️ 213 (Rochester)
✈️ 2374 (Ditton)

Over the course of the weekend, our Cadets threw themselves into a packed programme of expedition skills, including:
🗺️ Navigation Training — learning to read the land and find their way
🔥 Stove Training & Camp Craft — mastering life in the field
🎒 Food & Kit Training — preparing and packing like seasoned explorers

And the moment that made it all worthwhile? The weekend culminated in a remotely supervised navigation exercise, where each and every Cadet had the chance to put their new skills to the test and prove they are ready to progress to the next stage of their Duke of Edinburgh's Award expeditions. 🏅

The commitment, teamwork, and determination shown by ALL the Cadets this weekend has been truly outstanding — watching them grow in confidence over just two days has been a joy to see.

A massive thank you must go to all of the dedicated event staff who gave up their weekend to plan, deliver and support this training. Your expertise and passion for developing our young people does not go unnoticed — none of this happens without you. 👏

Well done to every single Cadet involved. Adventure awaits — onwards to the next stage! 🧭⛺

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc

@213squadronatc 
@25sqnrafac 
@1404_chatham_sqn_raf_aircadets

posts.pic_text_raw:
This week has been a busy week for our Squadron.

Firstly, CWO Callaghan-Jarvis joined fellow Cadets from Kent Wing to complete the world-famous Nijmegen Four Days Marches (International Vierdaagse Afstandsmarsen Nijmegen)! Over four grueling days, our cadets pushed through the all types of weather conditions, physical and psychological challenges to complete an astonishing 160 km (100 miles) through the Netherlands - all with smiles on their faces and incredible team spirit.

In addition to this, Cadets from the Squadron attended Farnborough Airshow.  Whilst there, the Cadets managed to charm their way to get to explore some of the fast jets of our NATO partners.

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc #nijmegenmarches #FarnboroughInternational

🌟 INCREDIBLE effort from our Cadets! 🌟

Friday night, the Cadets of the Squadron pulled on their boots, grabbed their sleeping bags, and took part in the Great Tommy Sleep Out — spending the night sleeping in tents to honour the sacrifice of our Armed Forces veterans. 🏕️🇬🇧

These young men and women didn't just show up — they stepped up, braving the cold to raise an outstanding...
💰 £600! 💰

We couldn't be more proud of every single one of them. The Great Tommy Sleep Out is a powerful reminder of what our veterans have endured, and our Cadets faced the challenge with courage, compassion, and the spirit that makes 40F Squadron so special.

A huge THANK YOU to everyone who sponsored, supported, and cheered our Cadets on — this achievement belongs to all of you too. 🙏

Well done to you all.

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc #greattommysleepout #rbve

🎉 85 Years of the Air Training Corps 🎉

On 5 February 1941, the Air Training Corps was officially formed. Today, we were proud to mark this historic milestone with a special anniversary service.

Cadets and staff from across the London & South East Region came together at St Clement Danes, the Central Church of the RAF and the RAF’s family church, to reflect on 85 years of service, opportunity, and development for young people.

Kent Wing was proudly represented by 81 cadets and 16 staff from across the Wing. Kent Wing cadets also played a key role in the service, contributing as members of the band, choir, and through the reading of prayers.

We were honoured to be joined by Dame Susan Langley, the Lady Mayor of London, alongside the Regional Commandant, Group Captain K Walton.

A fitting and memorable service to celebrate 85 years of the Air Training Corps, its people, and its continued impact across generations. #RAFAC85  #KentWing #AirCadets

This weekend saw over 60 Cadets from our Sector attend a Multi-Activity camp at Lydd.

Cadets had the opportunity to experience multiple activities, including paddlesports, mountain biking, fieldcraft, shooting, STEM, and archery.

For quite a few Cadets, this was their first camp, so allowed them to experience the etiquette of spending time on a military establishment and socialise with fellow Cadets.

The camp also provided the opportunity for Staff to refresh and continue to build their own skills in their respective knowledge areas.

Thanks to all of the Staff from the Sector, Wing and Region for supporting this event.

This weekend saw the final Nijmegen training weekend for the London & South East Region Nijmegen Teams. They have marched over 150 miles since January this year and have proven their teamwork, leadership, resilience and strength to be selected to represent the Region at the prestigious Nijmegen Four Days Marches in Holland, this July.

Sgt Callaghan-Jarvis joined 3 other Kent Wing  Cadets to take part in this event.  She has been selected to join fourteen other colleagues from across the Region to make up the two Teams representing LaSER RAFAC, as of the part of the official British Military Contingent in Holland. 

The Nijmegen 4Daagse (Four Days) March is the largest Road Marching event in the world and will see over 46,000 walkers cover a marathon distance walk every day for four days, with more than a million spectators cheering them on!

We wish the selected Cadets good luck for this year's Nijmegen March

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc

Recently, 7 cadets undertook the Bronze National Navigation Award Scheme.  The scheme provides them with the opportunity to develop their navigation skills in the countryside using paths, tracks, and other linear features, and also included basic map interpretation and compass work.

Well done to you all for completing the award.

posts.pic_text_raw:
Cadets and Staff from 40F Squadron joined Medway Squadrons and other Cadet Forces to take part in the Armed Forces Day parade at the Historic Dockyard, Chatham.

Cdt Pelivan & Cdt Malyan commented:

"It’s a great opportunity to feel part of wider military family .This day not only shows our respect to both current serving military personnel and veterans but also inspires young people to consider a career in the service or join organisations like Cadets.

Being a part of this day reinforces our pride of the Royal Air Force"

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc #ArmedForcesDay

posts.pic_text_raw:
Today saw 18 Staff and Cadets from the Squadron undertake the 14km North Downs Walk.

The North Downs Walk is organised by the Weald of Kent Rotary with the primary purpose of supporting Cancer Research UK.

2025 is a year with a lot of big anniversaries. Rotary International is 120 years old. Weald of Kent Rotary is celebrating their 50th anniversary. This was the 40th North Downs Walk (held every year since 1985, except 2020)

Well done to all those that took part and for raising money for both Cancer Research UK and the Squadron.

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc #wealdofkentrotary #rotaryinternational

Last weekend, three cadets from the Squadron attended RAF Kenley to undertake some Gliding Induction training.

Throughout the day, the Cadets got to experience both flying in the Viking glider and the launch and management of the gliders on the ground as they prepared and undertook their launch process.

We hope all the Cadets enjoyed their experience and look forward to seeing them develop their aviation experience in the future.

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc

posts.pic_text_raw:
Today, cadets from Maidstone competed against other squadrons within Kent at the Kent Wing Athletics competition at the Julie Rose stadium in Ashford. Despite the high temperatures, the standards were high, with Maidstone cadets taking home a number of medals and some cadets qualifying to represent Kent at the London & South East Region competition.  Special congratulations go to the under 15 boys team who took bronze in the 4 x 100m relay and the overall silver medal position.

 #whatwedo #laseraircadets #aircadets #kentwingatc
